clue.text: Lodging with club — perhaps this gets you through gate

definitions.text: perhaps this gets you through gate

parts.note: boarding is lodging, as in board and lodging
a club is one of the playing cards, so club can stand for card

explanation.surface: A traveller finds lodging with a club, and wonders what document will get them past the gate.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example, flagged by 'perhaps': the pass shown at an airport departure gate.
explanation.definitionFit: At an airport, the pass printed with your seat is what lets you through the departure gate to the plane.

clue.text: Bribe the French right? He'll make a mess of it!

definitions.text: He'll make a mess of it!

parts.note: a bung is British slang for a bribe
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether bribing the French would be right, and is warned the briber will make a mess of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy person who botches every job is the sort who will make a mess of things.

clue.text: Valuable resource of state with no end of power

indicators.note: with no tells us a letter is taken away from the word for state

parts.note: to state is to assert, to declare firmly

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word power

explanation.surface: A political note about a state's prized resource running out of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything of value owned by a person or company, such as property or a skill, is a useful holding.

clue.text: Identifies problem of San Diego's poor

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in bad shape and must be put into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the city name with its possessive S

explanation.surface: A report pinpointing the troubles of San Diego's poor people.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the possessive S is part of the fodder: all nine letters of San Diego's are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who identifies the problem from symptoms is naming the illness, the medical sense of the verb.

clue.text: Hacks in difficulty — leader appears finally

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word for difficulty is moved to the last position

parts.note: a snag is a difficulty or hitch

explanation.surface: Journalists in trouble, with the leader article only appearing at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hacks' looks like journalists, but here it means old horses; the S of SNAG moves to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack is a worn-out or hired horse, and old nags are the same sort of tired mount.

clue.text: Cleaner aims to develop personal quality

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British word for a cleaner

indicators.note: to develop suggests the letters of aims grow into a new form

explanation.surface: A cleaner sets goals to build up her personal qualities.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is the compelling personal charm that draws people to someone, a quality of personality.

clue.text: Puzzle of president mainly supporting soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so the soldiers sit below

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British soldiers

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so the final letter of the president's name is dropped

parts.note: Bush is a US president's surname

explanation.surface: A puzzle involving a president who is mostly backed by the army.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, the president's shortened name sits on top and RE (Royal Engineers) holds it up from below.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture puzzle in which images and letters stand for words is a well known kind of brain-teaser.

clue.text: Naturally connected with part of university curriculum

parts.note: of can mean connected with or concerning
a course is a unit of study in a university curriculum

explanation.surface: Something naturally linked to a module of a degree programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturally, used as an interjection, means certainly or as expected, the same as the stock phrase of agreement.

clue.text: Wait on minister after a time

indicators.note: after places the word for minister behind the letters for a time

parts.note: to minister to someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: A church minister waiting a while before being served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a clergyman, but it is a verb: to minister is to look after.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait on someone, as a servant does, is to serve or look after their needs.

clue.text: Lost again, lost in dreams of times past

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have gone astray and must be found in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lost once more, drifting in reveries of earlier days.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Lost' is fodder and the second is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A wistful longing for the past is exactly a dreaming about bygone days.

clue.text: Piece about lower socio-economic groups in suit

indicators.note: about means the word for piece goes around the letters for the groups

parts.note: a bit is a small piece
E and F are taken as letter grades low down the scale of social classes

explanation.surface: An article about poorer social classes appearing in a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like a noun (clothes or a court case) but it is the verb meaning to be right for.
explanation.definitionFit: To befit is to be fitting or appropriate for, as in a dress that suits the occasion.

clue.text: A canvas by Lowry originally undeveloped

indicators.note: originally picks out the opening letter of the painter's name

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas, so canvas can mean a tent

explanation.surface: An unfinished painting by L. S. Lowry, the English artist of industrial scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canvas' suggests a painting; here it is the fabric of a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something latent is present but hidden or not yet grown, like a talent waiting to emerge.

clue.text: Heart-throb may be strangely isolated

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of isolated are arranged oddly into a new word

explanation.surface: A film idol may lead a strangely lonely life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart-throb' wants to be a pin-up; read literally it is one beat of the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Diastole is the phase of the heartbeat when the heart relaxes and refills, part of each throb.

clue.text: Counter is covered by others

indicators.note: covered by means the word is sits inside the word for others

parts.note: the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A shop counter that is hidden under other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a noun but it is the verb, to oppose.
explanation.definitionFit: To counter an attack is to oppose or withstand it, which is to stand firm against it.

clue.text: Draw on gin distributed wholesale

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first part sits on top of the second

parts.note: a sweep, short for sweepstake, is a lottery draw

indicators.note: distributed says the letters of gin are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Gin handed out in bulk, drawn on for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesale changes are sweeping ones: broad and all-embracing, made across the board.

clue.text: Spoilt broadcast by one elected member

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an MP is a Member of Parliament, elected to the Commons
aired means broadcast, put on air

explanation.surface: A damaged programme broadcast by a single MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impaired is weakened or damaged, so it has been spoilt in quality.

clue.text: Four start going off such a surface

indicators.note: going off suggests the letters go wrong and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Four runners start racing on a particular kind of track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such a surface' points back at the clue: four runners starting on an artificial grass track.
explanation.definitionFit: This brand of artificial grass is a playing surface, the sort laid on sports pitches.

clue.text: Pre-match do top boxing news

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the word for top boxes in the letters for news

parts.note: height can mean the top or peak, as in the height of fashion
N is new, so news is read as two Ns

explanation.surface: A promoter's top boxing news ahead of a big match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pre-match' means before a marriage, not a fight; a hen night is the British party for a bride-to-be and her female friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A party held for a bride before her wedding is a celebration ahead of the match, the marriage.

clue.text: Manages abroad, according to reports

indicators.note: according to reports says we go by what is heard, a word that sounds the same

parts.note: overseas means abroad, in a foreign country

explanation.surface: A manager runs the foreign operations, or so it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage a project is to supervise it, watching over the work and directing it.

clue.text: Airport luggage belts lacking vehicle for fliers

indicators.note: lacking means the word for vehicle is removed from the belts

parts.note: carousels are the revolving belts in airport baggage halls
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Airport baggage belts without a car for passengers who have flown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fliers' suggests air passengers; it means birds. Ousels (ouzels) are blackbirds and their kin.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel is an old name for the blackbird and similar thrushes, so these are birds, creatures that fly.

clue.text: Flow of runs in second eleven, perhaps

indicators.note: in means the letter for runs goes inside the other letters

parts.note: an eleven is a cricket or football team, with 'perhaps' marking it as an example
R stands for runs in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A cricket report on the flow of runs scored by the second eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket eleven is a team; R is the scorecard abbreviation for runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook or a steady current of water is a flow, and the word also covers any steady flow of things.

clue.text: Damned wayward son is infuriating

indicators.note: wayward suggests the letters stray from their order and must be rearranged

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A cursed, wayward son is driving his parents mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To be driving someone mad with anger, as the verb does, is to be infuriating to them.

clue.text: Replace drink works

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
a plant is a works, a factory

explanation.surface: Someone orders the drinks at a factory to be swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To supplant someone is to take their place, ousting and replacing them.

clue.text: Thread of story about school being evacuated

indicators.note: about means the word for story goes around the other letters

parts.note: a lie is a story, a fib

indicators.note: being evacuated means the inside of the word school is emptied, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: The thread of a tale about pupils evacuated from a school, as in wartime Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, strong cotton thread, used especially for stockings.

clue.text: Taken into custody, managed to grab pie that is being dropped

indicators.note: to grab means the word for managed seizes the remaining letter inside it

parts.note: coped means managed

indicators.note: being dropped means the letters for that is are removed from pie

parts.note: pie is taken as written, before the removal
IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A suspect arrested after managing to snatch a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing IE ('that is') from PIE leaves P, which COPED grabs.
explanation.definitionFit: Copped is British slang for caught or arrested, so a thief who is copped has been taken in by the police.

clue.text: This girl exercises with a heartless rival

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of the word rival is removed, keeping its outside letters

explanation.surface: A girl works out alongside a cold-hearted rival.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearl is a girl's first name, so the clue's girl is one named example.

clue.text: Shock hospital broadcast

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
to air is to broadcast

explanation.surface: A hospital puts out shocking news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' looks like a surprise; it is a shock of hair, a thick mop.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock is a thick, bushy mass, as in a shock of red curls on someone's head.

clue.text: Joins golf club?

definitions.meaning: connects or couples together, as a chain is fastened
a seaside golf course; the question mark admits the stretch from course to club

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for connecting things and a name for a coastal golf course.

clue.text: Break down into small pieces, making aunt glare

indicators.note: making signals that the letters of aunt glare are used to make something new

explanation.surface: Breaking something into crumbs makes Auntie glare.
explanation.definitionFit: To granulate is to form into grains, crushing a substance into tiny particles.

clue.text: Female first possibly to welcome Universal's pictures

indicators.note: to welcome means the rearranged letters take the letter for Universal inside them
possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for Universal, suitable for all

explanation.surface: A women-first studio policy greeting Universal Pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating for Universal, suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictures is an old word for films, and full-length cinema films are the main pictures in a programme.
